PullRequest.Title: Engineering - fetch Chromium build scripts through the GitHub API with fallbacks
PullRequest.Body:
VS Code's Linux build fetches two Chromium scripts from raw.githubusercontent.com at build time: clang's `tools/clang/scripts/update.py` (`setup-env.sh`, on a node_modules cache miss) and `third_party/dpkg-shlibdeps/dpkg-shlibdeps.pl` (`Prepare deb package`). That host rate-limits **per network** ("too many requests from your network"), so on shared agent IPs neither a token nor short retries help during an outage.

Impact:
- **Releasing insider [489293](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=489293) (Oct 26 17:00):** `Prepare deb package` failed on Linux x64, arm64 and armhf after all 5 attempts from #343566 got 429, which blocked Publish. Earlier hits were 487937 and 487986 on Oct 22, so that's 3 official builds in 5 days.
- **Main CI [489263](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=489263):** 7 jobs failed at `Install dependencies`. `curl -s ... update.py | python -` fed the 429 page to Python, which failed with `SyntaxError: illegal target for annotation`.
- **GitHub PR CI:** 65 failed jobs across 15 runs in 30 days, 10 of those runs on Oct 26.

Changes:
- New `build/lib/chromiumSource.ts` downloads a file from the Chromium tree at the version pinned in `cgmanifest.json`. It tries these sources in order:
  1. the GitHub REST contents API (`api.github.com`, authenticated, per-token rate limit), when a token is set
  2. raw.githubusercontent.com, authenticated and then anonymous
  3. Chromium's Gitiles host
- It retries the whole set after 10, 30 and 60 s. Each request has a connect timeout and an overall deadline, and the file is written only if the content starts with `#!`. Headers, including the token, go through curl's config on stdin, and the log names the source that served the file.
- `calculate-deps.ts` uses it for `dpkg-shlibdeps.pl`, replacing the GitHub-only loop from #343566.
- `setup-env.sh` uses it for `update.py`, saves the script to a temp file and only then runs it. This also drops that file's second hard-coded copy of the Chromium version.

All sources serve byte-identical files at `150.0.7871.250`.

Gitiles is last because validation run 489314 showed it returning 403 to every request from the ADO Linux agents. It works from other networks.

Why not vendor the scripts: `dpkg-shlibdeps.pl` is GPL-2.0, which needs a licensing decision before it can live in this repo. A vendored `update.py` would also have to be re-copied on every Chromium bump, or clang would silently drift.

Validation:
- `node --test build/lib/test/chromiumSource.test.ts`: 5/5 pass. The tests cover source order with and without a token, Gitiles base64 decoding, error pages with a 200 status, and exhausting every round.
- `tsc` passes on the changed files, and `bash -n setup-env.sh` passes.
- A live run of the helper with a token fetched both scripts from `api.github.com` with the expected hashes.
- Def 111 Product runs build Linux x64, arm64 and armhf only, with publish and release off and tests skipped. Each runs on a throwaway branch with a bumped `.cachesalt`, so `setup-env.sh` runs cold:
  - Normal path: [489353](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=489353)
  - Forced failure: [489354](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=489354), with the API host broken, so the fallback has to serve both scripts.

> Authored with Copilot

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The source order, synchronous spawnSync call, 120-second deadline, and critical-path callers are explicit in the changed code. The exact frequency of a slow-but-not-fast-failing API endpoint is uncertain, but the latency mechanism and affected build paths are deterministic when it occurs.
Findings.PerformanceResource: serial network requests and blocked build-agent time
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Latency grows by up to 120 seconds for every earlier source that stalls before a healthy fallback; the cost is paid once per helper invocation, including independently in each Debian architecture job.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: blocked critical path and increased build latency
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Both callers contacted raw.githubusercontent.com directly. If raw GitHub was healthy, API-host degradation could not delay dependency setup or package preparation.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each download now waits for the newly preferred GitHub API request to finish or time out before trying the previously used raw GitHub URL. A slow API endpoint therefore delays a healthy raw fallback by up to 120 seconds.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added loop at build/lib/chromiumSource.ts:94-95 synchronously calls each source in order; getSources adds api.github.com before raw.githubusercontent.com, and curlGet gives each call a 120-second --max-time. Both changed callers now use this helper on their critical path.
Findings.Title: Fail over before a source can block for two minutes
Findings.Impact: When api.github.com is degraded or filtered but raw.githubusercontent.com is healthy, cold Linux dependency installation and each architecture's Prepare deb package step gain up to two minutes of avoidable critical-path latency. Multiple sequential degraded sources can compound this delay and consume a meaningful fraction of the 50-90 minute Linux job timeout.
Findings.Evidence: getSources places api.github.com first when the pipeline's GITHUB_TOKEN is present, then raw GitHub and Gitiles. downloadChromiumFile iterates these sources serially and curlGet uses spawnSync with --max-time 120. setup-env.sh invokes it before the clang update script during uncached x64 dependency setup, while calculate-deps.ts invokes it before the first dpkg-shlibdeps run during Debian package preparation. The pipelines provide GITHUB_TOKEN in both cases. Thus an API connection that stalls while raw.githubusercontent.com remains healthy blocks progress rather than failing over promptly.
Findings.Recommendation: Use a short per-source failover deadline (or hedge the next source after a short delay) while retaining the longer overall retry budget, so a healthy fallback is reached quickly without removing resilience.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold Linux x64 dependency installation and clang provisioning
Scenarios.CriticalPath: downloadChromiumFile must finish before update.py can run, and update.py must finish before npm dependency installation. All helper retries and fallback probes are therefore on the cold setup critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start Node to resolve the pinned Chromium version and download update.py.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One Node subprocess per cold x64 setup, introduced to run the helper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The shell invoked curl directly and piped its output to Python, without this Node process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the shell before the clang update script can execute.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch update.py from GitHub API, authenticated/anonymous raw GitHub, or Gitiles.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one API curl with a token; on failures up to four serial sources per round and four rounds, for at most 16 curl subprocess/network requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One direct raw.githubusercontent.com curl was attempted; API and Gitiles were not contacted and API degradation could not delay a healthy raw request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Every request and 10/30/60-second backoff blocks dependency setup; each request may run for 120 seconds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run Chromium update.py to provision the clang toolchain.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One Python process; its own clang download behavior depends on the existing script and local .build/CR_Clang state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same script ran from curl's stdout rather than a temporary file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before npm installation, but its placement and download behavior are unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch and extract client and remote sysroots when their directories are absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to two sysroot fetch workflows on cache misses before the changed helper path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical cache checks and downloads occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These complete before clang setup and remain on the cold setup path, but were not added or moved by the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One invocation per cold x64 dependency-install job; latency scales with the number of earlier stalled sources and rounds, not with npm package count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Sources and retry rounds are fully serialized by spawnSync and Atomics.wait. Separate CI jobs may execute independently in parallel, with no shared limiter or coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The setup step runs only on a node_modules cache miss; a warm cache skips setup-env.sh entirely. Within a cold run the Chromium script itself is not cached, although update.py may reuse the existing .build/CR_Clang output. The new helper has no positive or negative cross-process cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: token presence, API-first ordering, synchronous execution, timeout values, cache gating, and downstream ordering are explicit in repository code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: API-only degradation frequency and observed timeout duration vary by network; fast HTTP failures cost little, while a connected but stalled endpoint can consume the full 120 seconds. The helper is skipped on warm node_modules cache hits.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity latency regression: the newly preferred API probe can serialize up to 120 seconds ahead of the previously healthy raw source.

Scenarios.Scenario: Prepare Debian packages for x64, arm64, and armhf
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Sysroot resolution, the Chromium script download, and every dpkg-shlibdeps subprocess must complete before dependency validation and Debian package preparation can continue.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve and, on a cache miss, install the Chromium Debian sysroot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sysroots.json curl per package preparation; tarball network download and extraction only when its stamp cache misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same request, stamp check, download, and extraction behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes dependency calculation but is unchanged by this PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve and install the VS Code sysroot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero network fetches on a valid stamp; otherwise one GitHub release metadata request plus one asset download, each with existing retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same stamp cache and download path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before dependency calculation but is unchanged by this PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch dpkg-shlibdeps.pl through the API/raw/Gitiles source set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one API curl; on total failure up to 16 serial curl requests with a token. The result is reused for every binary in the same process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One script download per process was already cached, but it used up to five raw-GitHub curl attempts; it never waited on an API probe before a healthy raw request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first dependency calculation blocks on all probes and backoffs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate native modules and calculate shared-library dependencies.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One find subprocess plus one Perl dpkg-shlibdeps subprocess for each discovered native module and four fixed executables.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same effective file cardinality and serial Perl execution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serially computes package dependencies after the shared script is available; unchanged by the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and retain a process-local script file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One temporary directory/file per package-preparation process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old implementation likewise created one temporary directory and script path per process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous filesystem work before the script download; not a material regression.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One helper invocation per Debian package process/architecture after process-local deduplication; fallback latency scales with stalled sources and rounds, while unchanged Perl work scales with discovered native binaries plus four fixed executables.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The helper's source requests and retry rounds are serial. Per-binary Perl subprocesses are also serial through files.map. The x64, arm64, and armhf package jobs can run concurrently in CI without a shared request limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The downloaded dpkg-shlibdeps path is cached only in the module-level variable for one Node process, so all binaries in that package preparation share one download. There is no cross-job or cross-process Chromium-script cache. Chromium and VS Code sysroots use stamp files for tarball reuse, although Chromium's sysroots.json is still fetched on each invocation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: process-level coalescing, API-first source order, serial curl execution, retry cardinality, and the package pipeline token are all directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of native modules controls unchanged Perl work, not download count. API stall prevalence and duration are uncertain; three architecture jobs can experience the delay independently and concurrently.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable API-first failover latency; no additional finding for per-binary work because the download remains correctly coalesced once per process and the Perl fan-out is pre-existing.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and traced both production build workflows. Submitted one medium-severity finding for serial two-minute source probes ahead of healthy fallbacks. No cache-retention, allocation, repeated-download, or aggregate-concurrency regression met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
